title: How Much Does It Cost to Remove Old Carpet or Flooring Before Hardwood Installation?
meta: Old floor removal is a separate line from the $3.25 per sq ft hardwood install labor. What carpet, vinyl, tile and hardwood tear-out involves in Seattle.
keywords: cost to remove old carpet before hardwood, flooring removal cost Seattle, tear out tile before hardwood floors, remove old hardwood floor cost, carpet removal and disposal, hardwood installation cost Seattle
offers: Hardwood floor installation, engineered or solid

blocks.lead: Removal is a separate line on a hardwood quote. Wills Flooring's $3.25 per sq ft installation labor covers laying the new floor; tearing out carpet, vinyl, tile or old hardwood and hauling it away is quoted at the free estimate once we see what is down and what is under it.
blocks.detail: Carpet is the cheapest and fastest to remove. Glued sheet vinyl and mortared tile are the slowest and cost the most. Pre-1980 sheet vinyl can need asbestos testing before anyone touches it.

blocks.html: Seattle houses hide their history in layers. A Beacon Hill bungalow might have carpet over 1970s sheet vinyl over original fir. A Green Lake remodel might have tile mortared to a plywood underlayment screwed to the subfloor. Each layer changes how long removal takes, what gets hauled to the transfer station, and whether the subfloor underneath is ready for hardwood. That is why we do not print a single removal rate: the honest price depends on what the pry bar finds. This post shows what each type of removal involves, how it fits next to our published installation labor, and when you should pull the old floor yourself.

blocks.note: National averages for carpet removal alone run about $1 to $2 per sq ft including disposal. That is an industry figure, not a Wills price; we quote your actual floor.

blocks.text: Why we quote removal at the estimate instead of a flat rate

items.title: We do not know how many layers there are
items.text: One Wallingford kitchen we did had four floors stacked: vinyl plank, sheet vinyl, particleboard underlayment and linoleum. A flat per-foot rate would have been wrong in either direction. At the estimate we lift a register grate or a threshold and count.

items.title: Asbestos changes everything
items.text: Sheet vinyl, 9 in tiles and their black mastic from before about 1980 can contain asbestos. We do not sand, grind or rip them. If a test comes back positive, licensed abatement handles removal and we install afterward, often over a new underlayment rather than the old material.

items.title: The subfloor sets the real price
items.text: Removal ends when the subfloor is clean, flat and sound. Tile jobs often leave a cracked or overscrewed underlayment. Old carpet hides water damage at exterior doors. Repairs are their own line, and we would rather show you than guess.

items.title: Seattle access
items.text: A dumpster needs a spot on a Ballard street with permit parking. A Capitol Hill condo means an elevator reservation and bagging debris. Those are real hours and they belong in your quote, not on the final invoice as a surprise.

blocks.note: This is installation labor only. Material, removal of the old floor and subfloor repairs are quoted at the free in-home estimate.

blocks.text: Should you tear it out yourself?

a.title: Makes sense when
items: It is carpet and pad over plywood, and you own a utility knife and pliers
You have a truck or a dumpster and a free weekend
You pull every staple and tack strip nail, not just the carpet
You leave the underlayment and subfloor in place for us to inspect

b.title: Do not DIY when
items: It is sheet vinyl or 9 in tile from before 1980
It is tile: the dust and the demolition hammer are not a weekend project
There may be radiant tubing or old wiring under the floor
It is original fir or oak that might be worth refinishing instead

blocks.text: Mistakes that turn a cheap tear-out into an expensive one

items.html: Ripping up old vinyl without a test. A lab test is cheap. Disturbing asbestos tile in an occupied Seattle house is not.

Throwing away a floor you could have kept. Original 1920s fir in Queen Anne and Wallingford is often sound under carpet. Refinishing at $3.99 per sq ft can cost less than removal plus new hardwood. Read what is under my carpet first.
Tearing out too early. New hardwood needs to acclimate in the house for several days. Living on bare subfloor with staples for two weeks is unpleasant and dangerous with kids.
Leaving the staples. Every pad staple left in the plywood is a high spot under new hardwood and a squeak later. Pulling them is most of the labor in carpet removal.
Putting carpet at the curb. Seattle does not collect it with regular garbage. It goes to a transfer station by weight, or in our truck.
Know the age of every layer. If the house or the flooring predates 1980, ask for a test before anyone cuts into vinyl.
Get removal, disposal and subfloor prep as separate written lines. Our estimate lists each one so you can compare quotes fairly and see what you would save by doing part of it yourself.
Decide who moves what. Appliances, pianos and built-ins all need a plan before the crew arrives.
Sort out parking and access. A dumpster permit on a Seattle street or an elevator booking in a condo takes days, not hours.
Ask what happens if the subfloor is bad. We stop, show you, and price the repair before continuing. See our hardwood installation page for what the install itself includes.

faq.q: Is removal included in the $3.25 per sq ft hardwood installation price?
faq.a: No. The $3.25 covers labor to install engineered or solid hardwood, with a 500 sq ft minimum. Material, removal of the old floor, disposal and subfloor prep are separate lines quoted at the free in-home estimate, because they depend on what is actually on your floor.

faq.q: How much does it cost to remove carpet before installing hardwood in Seattle?
faq.a: Wills Flooring quotes it after seeing the floor, since staple count, stairs and access change the hours. Industry averages for carpet removal with disposal run roughly $1 to $2 per sq ft nationally, but that is a general figure, not our price. It is the cheapest floor type to remove.

faq.q: Can new hardwood go over the old floor instead of removing it?
faq.a: Sometimes. Hardwood can go over sound existing hardwood or a flat, well-adhered vinyl in some cases, but never over carpet, and height at doors and stairs becomes a problem. Removal is usually the better result, and it lets us inspect the subfloor.

faq.q: What if my old flooring has asbestos?
faq.a: We stop and recommend a lab test. If it is positive, a licensed abatement contractor removes it, or it can sometimes be left in place and covered with a new underlayment. We install afterward. Sheet vinyl, 9 in tiles and black mastic from before about 1980 are the usual suspects in Seattle homes.

faq.q: Should I remove the old carpet myself to save money?
faq.a: If it is carpet over plywood and you pull every staple and tack strip nail, yes, it saves a real line on the quote. Leave tile, old vinyl and anything that might be original hardwood to us. Do not tear out until the new hardwood has been delivered and acclimated.

faq.q: How long does removal add to a hardwood installation?
faq.a: Carpet on a 900 sq ft main floor adds a few hours. Glued vinyl or tile can add a full day or two, plus subfloor repair. We schedule removal, prep and installation as one job so the house is torn up for the shortest possible time.
